summary: This article explains how mangrove trees survive in salty coastal water, why they matter to sea life and coasts, and how Saudi Arabia is planting them.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “Mangrove Forests: Trees That Live in the Sea”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: the regular rising and falling of the sea, usually twice a day
a gas in the air that living things need to breathe
a very young plant that has grown from a seed

challengeTerms.def: a feature that helps a living thing survive in its environment
sand, mud, and small pieces of rock carried and dropped by water or wind
a part of a plant, such as a young sprouting seed, that can grow into a new plant

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that planting mangroves is one of the best ways to protect our coasts? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how mangroves are able to survive in salty, muddy coastal water.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review tide, oxygen, and seedling, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use adaptation, sediment, and propagule in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
